summary: Micronesia needs no visa or permit for visits of 30 days or less from citizens of essentially every country; longer stays need an entry permit. US citizens go further still: under the Compact of Free Association they may enter, live and work in the FSM without a visa.

AF.notes: No visa or permit is needed for visits of 30 days or less: complete the Customs, Immigration & Quarantine (CIQ) form on arrival, and bring a passport valid at least 120 days beyond your date of entry and a return or onward ticket. To stay longer, an entry permit for up to 60 more days is required from the FSM Division of Immigration.

safety.text: Serious crime against visitors is rare and island communities are welcoming. The practical risks are alcohol-related trouble after dark, occasional theft from unlocked rooms, weak road lighting, and how far you are from advanced medical care.

tips.text: Bring enough US dollars in cash: the UK FCDO says ATM facilities are limited, and Canada says there are few ATMs.
Canada's travel advice says to dress conservatively, behave discreetly and respect religious and social traditions. It also says drunkenness and drinking in public places are punishable offences.

Canada's travel advice says unexploded World War II ordnance may pose a risk: if you dive or boat, avoid doing so after daylight hours, keep away from areas where sunken vessels or planes have been reported, and do not touch war remnants. Removing anything from a World War II wreck is illegal.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Micronesia?
faq.answer: Almost certainly not. Citizens of essentially every country need neither a visa nor a permit for visits of 30 days or less, provided they hold a passport valid at least 120 days beyond the date of entry and a return or onward ticket; stays over 30 days need an entry permit. US citizens need no visa under the Compact of Free Association, and their entry permit can cover the whole visit, up to one year.

faq.question: What does the Compact of Free Association mean for US citizens?
faq.answer: Under the Compact, US citizens may enter the Federated States of Micronesia without a visa, and FSM citizens have the same right in the United States. A US passport or a birth certificate proves citizenship, and the entry permit covers the length of the visit, up to one year. You still pass through immigration, and local rules on employment and land ownership apply.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than 30 days in Micronesia?
faq.answer: Yes. Visitors staying longer than 30 days need an entry permit from the FSM Division of Immigration, which may be issued for an additional period of up to 60 days. Apply before your first 30 days end.

faq.question: Do I need any vaccinations for Micronesia?
faq.answer: None is required for entry: the FSM is not on WHO's list of countries that ask for a yellow fever certificate, and no FSM authority publishes a vaccination rule. Routine vaccinations should be up to date; dengue outbreaks occur, so mosquito precautions matter more than paperwork.
